licence.note: Written only by this build: one row per connection at spawn ('tool hygiene ON: mode=on (TOOL_HYGIENE unset)'). The fleet (c6e91a8) has no _tool_hygiene, _redundant_craft, _craft_admit or _worn_first row.

require.name: stone_pickaxe craft rows (the population the refusal targets)

draw_exposure.note: craft rows whose detail names stone_pickaxe ('crafted 1x stone_pickaxe', 'cannot craft stone_pickaxe -- ...'). Every pool digs stone, so part 2's population is fleet-wide; the census (10-07 17:31Z) found 163 worn copies in 80 bags, 133 beside a keeper.

exposure.note: Ready = >= 5 canary _redundant_craft rows AND >= 1 canary _craft_admit row AND OBSERVED canary worn-first wear (snapshots: a <= 10-use copy wore while the fullest same-name copy stayed) >= 3 intervals AND above the control's per-bot-h rate (the deployed toolFor cannot produce that pattern, so the control's ~0.05/bot-h is noise from dig paths outside toolFor) AND >= 1 canary _worn_first row AND both positive controls >= 1 (control admitted redundant crafts by the same rule over the decision stream: 59-67 per 6 h on 70 bots in the dry runs; control wear beside a copy the hygiene rule opens: ~2,700-2,900 per 6 h). Expected ~0.15-0.17 admitted redundant crafts per control bot-h -> ~10 refusals per 10 canary bots per 6 h; part 2: 95 of 155 worn copies in 31 of 80 bags drainable (census 10-07 18:04Z).

own_lines.note: LIVENESS: canary _tool_hygiene ON rows. BLOCKS KEEP (INCONCLUSIVE).
Arms: the control writes no _tool_hygiene, _redundant_craft, _craft_admit or _worn_first row. BLOCKS KEEP.
LIVENESS (G1's population): canary _craft_admit rows exist, so a G1 of 0 is a measurement, not a silent instrument. BLOCKS KEEP (INCONCLUSIVE).
The switch: a canary row saying 'tool hygiene off' (the fleet env sets nothing; the default is on).

G1: a canary _craft_admit that the read's independent rule (given the row's logged wanted set) calls redundant, judged on the row's own snapshot (same tick as the check). Exit-contract rounding edge (y rounded to 0.1) is never a breach. The exit-shortfall memory (mine's refusal for want of swings, 15 min) is re-derived from the bot's own _exit_reserve_abort rows and reset at each _tool_hygiene row (a new process).

G2: a canary _redundant_craft the rule does not justify from its own snapshot (no same-or-better cover at need, fewer than 2 usable pickaxes, exit-short at the snapshot's y, no carried station). Unknown-durability copies count full. The exit-shortfall memory (mine's refusal for want of swings, 15 min) is re-derived from the bot's own _exit_reserve_abort rows and reset at each _tool_hygiene row (a new process).

G3: a canary _worn_first whose logged pick context does not justify the chosen copy (<= 1 use outside last swings; a worn copy without a same-or-higher keeper above FLOOR and two other DEPOSIT-PROOF copies -- every copy at 2..10 plus one copy above FLOOR per name; a more-worn same-name copy the rule opens).
G4: a refusal whose own logged wanted set holds the item, whose task is craft_<item>_*, or whose source is a work order (a refusal the task needed: the dead end the rule exists to prevent).
POSITIVE CONTROL (part 1): the same rule finds admitted redundant crafts in the control's decision stream. BLOCKS KEEP.

POSITIVE CONTROL (part 2): control wear intervals where the fullest copy wore beside a more-worn copy the hygiene rule would OPEN (keeper + deposit survivors; the two-copy spare does not count). BLOCKS KEEP.
